title: {{term:circle}}s: radius, diameter and π
summary: Measure the diameter and radius of a circle. Wrap a tape round a circle and find how many diameters make the circumference.
guide: A {{term:diameter}} is a straight line through the {{term:centre}} of a circle, from one side to the other.
A {{term:radius}} goes from the centre to the circle. A diameter is two radii: diameter = 2 × radius.
The {{term:circumference}} is the distance all the way round a circle. Wrap a string or tape round it, unroll it and measure it with a ruler.
The circumference of every circle is about 3.14 times its diameter. This number is called pi, written π.
Drag the ruler so its 0 is at the start of what you measure.

radius.title: The radius
radius.prompt: Drag the ruler and measure the diameter of this circle. Now: what is the radius in centimetres?
radius.hint: Put the 0 of the ruler under one end of the diameter. Read the diameter. The radius is half of it.
radius.success: Well done! The diameter is 4 cm and the radius is half of it: 2 cm.
radius.why: Why is the radius half the diameter?
radius.model: The diameter goes through the centre. From one end to the centre is a radius, and from the centre to the other end is another radius. So diameter = 2 × radius, and radius = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

feedback.diameter: 4 cm is the diameter. The radius goes from the centre to the circle: half the diameter.
feedback.doubled: You doubled the diameter. The radius is smaller than the diameter: half of it.
feedback.not-from-zero: The circle does not start at the 0 of the ruler. Drag the ruler first.
feedback.not-aligned: The 0 of the ruler is not under the end of the diameter. Drag the ruler and measure again.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. The radius is half the diameter.
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. Read the diameter carefully first.

tape-around.title: A tape round a tin
tape-around.prompt: Maryam wrapped a tape once round a tin and unrolled it. The tin is 3 cm across. How long is the tape, the tin's circumference? Give one decimal place.
tape-around.hint: The tape starts at 0. See which number the end is just past, then count the small marks. Each small mark is 0.1 cm (1 mm).
tape-around.success: Well done! The tape is about 9.4 cm. The circumference is about 3 times the diameter.
tape-around.why: The circumference is longer than the diameter. About how many times longer?
tape-around.model: The diameter is 3 cm and the circumference is about 9.4 cm. Three diameters make 9 cm, so the circumference is a little more than 3 diameters.

feedback.diameter: 3 cm is the tin's diameter. Read the length of the tape on the ruler.
feedback.doubled: 6 cm is two diameters. The tape is much longer. Look at its end on the ruler.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. Look at the end of the tape again.
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. Look at the end of the tape again.
feedback.empty: Write the length of the tape.

how-many-diameters.title: How many diameters round?
how-many-diameters.prompt: At the top is the tape (the tin's circumference, 9.42 cm); below it is the diameter (3 cm). Work out circumference ÷ diameter, to two decimal places.
how-many-diameters.hint: Work out 9.42 ÷ 3. 3 × 3 = 9, and 0.42 is left over.
how-many-diameters.success: Well done! 9.42 ÷ 3 = 3.14. That is the number pi (π).
how-many-diameters.why: If you measured a bigger circle, what would circumference ÷ diameter be?
how-many-diameters.model: About 3.14 again. In every circle, big or small, the circumference is about 3.14 times the diameter. So we write: circumference = π × diameter.

feedback.whole-only: 3 is close, but the circumference is a bit more than 3 diameters. Divide the remainder too.
feedback.upside-down: You divided the diameter by the circumference. Divide the circumference by the diameter: 9.42 ÷ 3.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. Work out 9.42 ÷ 3 again.
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. Work out 9.42 ÷ 3 again.

pool.title: Round the circle
pool.prompt: The radius of this circle is 3 cm. Use π to work out its circumference: circumference = 3.14 × diameter.
pool.hint: First find the diameter: diameter = 2 × radius. Then multiply it by 3.14.
pool.success: Well done! The diameter is 6 cm, and 6 × 3.14 = 18.84 cm.
pool.why: Why must you find the diameter first?
pool.model: π tells us how many times the diameter fits round the circle, not the radius. So first I double the radius: 2 × 3 = 6. Then 6 × 3.14 = 18.84.

feedback.used-radius: You multiplied the radius by 3.14. The circumference is 3.14 times the diameter. Find the diameter first.
feedback.area: That is the area of the circle, not its circumference. Circumference = 3.14 × diameter.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. The diameter is 2 × 3.
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. The diameter is 2 × 3.
